item.title: Modi Puts India Firmly in the Israel-US Camp
item.description: Modi's strong support for Israel – and refusal to condemn the Israel-U.S. strikes on Iran, a long-time friend of India’s – have “diminished India’s stature in the eyes of the world.”

item.title: Central Asia’s ‘Soft Confederation’ Has a Hard Limit
item.description: The recent burst of C5+ summitry does not prove that Central Asia is on a linear path toward deep integration. The region is building something subtler and more durable.

item.title: China’s February 26 Military Purge: The Domino Effect
item.description: In the latest sign of continuing purges in China's military, 10 PLA officers were stripped of their roles as delegates to the National People’s Congress.

item.title: Japan’s Iran Dilemma: Oil, Alliances, and Nuclear Double Standards
item.description: For Japan, the crisis is not only about energy security. It also strikes at the heart of the country’s moral and strategic identity.

item.title: South Korean President Pledges to Respect North’s System in March 1st Address
item.description: Lee Jae-myung seeks peaceful coexistence with North Korea and shuttle diplomacy with Japan amid a shifting regional security landscape.

item.title: Central Asia Watches, Worries, as Conflict Threatens to Engulf the Middle East
item.description: It’s awkward to be on record calling Trump the “president of peace” as he plunges the Middle East into a likely catastrophic conflict.

item.title: How Former Allies Pakistan and the Taliban Came to ‘Open War’
item.description: For the first time, Pakistan has directly targeted the Afghan Taliban in cross-border strikes.

item.title: North Korea’s Response to the Israel-US Attacks on Iran
item.description: Just a week after North Korea signaled openness to dialogue, the U.S. launched a military operation against Iran with a stated goal of regime change.

item.title: Uzbekistan’s Afghanistan Push Accelerates
item.description: With growing trade volumes, infrastructure initiatives, and initial geological explorations in Afghanistan, Uzbekistan is testing whether economic interdependence and proximity can function as a substitute for political recognition.

item.title: The Decapitation of Iran: What Tehran’s Chaos Means for China
item.description: The joint Israeli-U.S. decapitation of the Iranian regime signals the end of China’s “Westward March” and a blow to its global influence.
